question: The Mahabodhi Temple was built entirely from______by Ashoka
solution:
The correct answer is__** bricks**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mahabodhi Temple was built from brick and stone by Emperor Ashoka i**n the 3rd century BC.
 
• The temple is** located in Bodh Gaya, Bihar, India.**
 
• The Mahabodhi Temple is **one of the oldest Buddhist temples** in India that is still standing. 
 
• The temple is **considered a fine example of Indian brickwork and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. **
 
• The** temple's design influenced the development of later architectural tradition**s. 
 
• The temple complex includes **the main temple, the Bodhi Tree, the Lotus Pond, and other ancient shrines. **​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Vast Empire of Ashoka**

 
 
• Born to the second Maurya**n emperor, Bindusara, and a grandson to the first emperor, Chandragupta Maurya, Ashoka was also referred to as Ashoka the Great.**
 
• **Ashoka's reign covered the majority of the Indian subcontinent, excluding some parts of Tamil Nadu and Kerala, from 268 B.C.E to 232 B.C.E.**
 
• **He successfully carried forward the legacy of his grandfather, Chandragupta Maurya, by expanding the empire further.**
 
• **His empire stretched from present-day Bangladesh in the east to Afghanistan in the west.**
 
• **Pataliputra, modern-day Patna, served as the capital of Ashoka's empire.**
 
• **The empire's provincial capitals included Takshash**ila (later known as Taxila) and Ujjain.
